svg.title: AD CLICK AGGREGATOR: sketchnote
svg.text: Clicks are money, so the numbers must be fast for dashboards and exact for
Redirect immediately and publish the click to
Kafka; never aggregate raw rows at query time.
A stream processor counts clicks per ad per
minute and writes them to a column store for
Deduplicate by a signed impression ID, and
recount from raw logs in a nightly batch job for
Click on an ad redirects the user to the advertiser
Advertisers query click metrics over time (minute
Never lose or double-count clicks (it is billing)
Aggregated rows: ads × minutes, which is small.
A 10k/s peak is easy for Kafka.
Naive: insert each click into Postgres and GROUP BY at query
time. Slow queries, and writes compete with reads.
Click service redirects immediately and publishes to Kafka.
Flink aggregates per (ad, minute) on event time and
upserts into an OLAP column store.
Idempotency: every impression gets a signed unique ID
when the ad is served; Flink dedupes on it, so double-clicks
and retries count once and forged clicks are rejected.
Lambda-style safety net: raw clicks to S3; a nightly batch
recount corrects aggregates, because billing must be
Checkpoints + Kafka offsets give replay; the sink upserts (ad_id, minute), so replays
Key on ad_id:random(0..N) to spread across partitions, then aggregate twice.
Streams give fast numbers; batch from immutable raw data gives exact billing numbers.
Column store and pre-aggregates make time-range queries over billions of rows
Aggregating raw rows at query time in the OLTP
Adding parts before a number shows they are
"A stream processor counts clicks per ad per minute
and writes them to a column store for fast queries."
